legend.text: Each lightning flash is a plucked hit. Left and right is where it is, higher means further north, louder means bigger. More hits means more lightning.
A steady note plays three times a second. It is higher when more storms are north of the equator.
More of the map flashing: louder, brighter steady notes.
The steady note leans toward where most flashes are, west on the left, east on the right.

mappings.label: Flashes north of the equator
mappings.why: Share of flash pixels in the northern hemisphere: northern summer storms = higher steady notes, southern = lower.

mappings.label: Map area flashing
mappings.why: Total flash area in the 10-day window: more storms = louder, brighter steady notes.

mappings.label: Longitude of the flash centre
mappings.why: Where most flashes are, west (left) to east (right), within this excerpt.

events.why: New flash blobs (threshold on yellow + connected components). The largest ones per sample become plucked hits, at most 8 per second: size = loudness (3 steps), longitude = left/right, latitude = pitch (north = higher). The rhythm of the hits IS the lightning.
